rules.sentence: Chronic, progressive renal failure remains a central feature of oculocerebrorenal syndrome and necessitates regular monitoring of renal function.
By the fourth decade of life, the majority of patients reach stage 4 to 5 chronic kidney disease.[35][37]
Musculoskeletal manifestations of oculocerebrorenal syndrome include osteopenia, tenosynovitis, and debilitating arthropathy.[38]
Osteopenia can be exacerbated by hypophosphatemia and metabolic acidosis, further resulting in pathologic fractures.[4]
These patients are also prone to stunted growth and short stature, which has been postulated to be the result of growth hormone deficiency.[39]
Scoliosis has also been reported in these patients and may worsen with age.[40]
